 JUDGMENT

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road accident dated 26.09.2021.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:
On 26.09.2021 when the petitioner was crossing the road with care and cautiousness by observing the vehicles plying in front of Tomato Mandi, N.Vaddahalli Village,
NH75 Road, near Road divider, a Two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA 07S8499 came with high speed in a rash ridden by its rider in a negligent manner, endangering human life and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to the said accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Mulbagal Gov. Hospital wherein he took first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to R.L.Jalappa Hospital then shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bangalore wherein he took treatment as an inpatient from 27.09.2021 to 14.10.2021, undergone operation left tibia, left clavicle and L4 vertebral body fracture under GA on 01.10.2021 and discharged with advice.
So far he has spent Rs.5,00,000/ towards treatment and other medical expenses.
3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, before the accident he was hale and healthy, working as a Laborer and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/ per month.
Due to accidental injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident he is unable to attend his work due to the disability.
The accident was due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the offending vehicle.
The Nangali Police have registered a case in Cr.No.125/2021 p/u/Sec.279 and 337 of IPC.
The 1 st respondent being the RC owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA07S8499 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, this petition.
4. In response to notice issued by this tribunal, the Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of summons, Respondent No.1 did not appear before this court hence, placed exparte.

5. The objections of the Respondent No.2:
It has denied all the averments of the petition and also denied the issuance of policy in respect of the Two wheeler bearing NO.KA07X8499.
The rider of the motorcycle did not have valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.
There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
There was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.

Further denied the age, income, avocation, medical expenses etc.,
and further stated that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence prayed for dismissal of the petition.

Ismail vs G.S.Narayana on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83602092/
2 6.

On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident took place on 26.09.2021 at about 7.00pm infront of Tomato Mandi, N.Vaddahalli Village, NH75 Road, Mulbagal Taluk, Kolar, due to rash and negligent act of riding of rider of Two Wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA07S8499 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation? If so, what is the quantum?
From whom payable?
3. What order or award?
7. The Petitioner in order to prove his case, has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 11 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.11.
Dr.Nagaraj B.N. - Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center was examined as PW.2 and got marked 2 documents as per Exs.P.12 & P.13.
He has also examined Mr.Kishor M.R.  MRO at RL Jalappa Hospital as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.14 to 17.
Mr.Nagaraja G.V.  MRO at Victoria Hospital, Bangalore got examined as PW.4 and got marked Exs.P.18 to 21.
On the other side, the Respondents did not examine any witness nor examined any witness.
8. Heard the arguments of the learned counsels for both the parties.

9. On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows: Issue No.1: In the affirmative, Issue No.2: In the affirmative, Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following: REASONS 10.
Issue No.1:

In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the Motorcycle, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 6 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.6.
PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit in lieu of his chief examination.
On the other hand the Respondent No.2 has denied the negligence on the part of the rider of the Motorcycle.
During the crossexamination of PW.1, nothing worth is elicited to show the absence of negligence on the part of the rider of the Motorcycle.

He has also got examined MROs of R.L.Jalappa Hospital, Bangalore and Victoria Hospital, Bangalore as PWs.3 & 4 and got marked Exs.P.14 to 21 authorization letter, police intimation, MLC register extract and copy of case sheet and authorization letter, MLC register extract,
case sheet with police intimation and Xray 2 in Nos. respectively.
During the cross examination of PWs.3 & 4, nothing worthwhile is elicited.

11. Moreover the documents produced at Exs.P.1 to 7 i.e., FIR with complaint, spot Mahazar, spot sketch, IMV report and charge sheet shows that there is negligence on the part of the rider of the Motorcycle.
There is no contrary evidence produced by the respondent No.2.
The IMV report shows that there was damage to the front right side crash guard and right side rear view mirror damaged.

Ismail vs G.S.Narayana on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83602092/
3
Therefore it is clear that the Motorcycle hit the petitioner and caused the accident and the petitioner suffered injuries as per Ex.P.5 wound certificate.
The accident occurred on 26.09.2021 at 7.00pm and FIR was registered after Two days i.e., on 28.09.2021 at 9.00pm on the complaint of petitioner himself.
Therefore, there is nothing to disbelieve the version of the petitioner.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.5 and discharge summary as per Ex.P.8.

They are all in connect with each other and it states that the petitioner has suffered lacerated wound over anterior aspect of proximal 1/3rd of right lower limb exposing underlying tissue, puncture wounds of over anteromedial and lateral aspect of proximal 3rd of left lower limb, laceration over right frontal region and abrasion over right frontal region which are grievous and simple in nature.
13. The petitioner has got examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N.  Orthopedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center, Bangalore as PW.2.

entities.text: Sai Ortho and Dental Center, Bangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He has deposed the details of surgery undergone by the petitioner and has stated that the petitioner has suffered physical disability of the left lower limb at 38%, physical disability of the right lower limb at 43% and to the whole body disability at 29%.
During his cross examination, he has admitted that he has not treated the petitioner.
The fractures are united.
Implants are in situ in the right leg and implants are removed from the left leg.
The clavicle fracture was treated conservatively and petitioner can walk independently.
There is no loss of power and ROM at the hips, no complications at the fracture site.

Disability:
14.
On perusal of the evidence of PW.2 and the Xray at Ex.P.13 it is clear that the petitioner has sustained clavicle fracture.
However he has claimed to be working as a Labor.

Therefore, the fracture of left leg both bones and right leg 1/3rd both bones, fracture of clavicle and L4 vertebra will effect his work and he will be unable to stand and work and also to lift things.
Therefore, considering his age and work, this Tribunal deems it fit to fix the functional disability at 50%.

Monthly income:
15.
The petitioner has stated that he is doing Labor work and earning Rs.30,000/ per month.
However, he has not examined any witness nor produced any Bank statement and any other documents in support of it.
The accident occurred in the year 2021.
Therefore, this Tribunal deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.15,000/ per month.
16. At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 46 years as could be made out from Ex.P.7/Notarized copy of Aadhar Card.
He was hale and healthy before the accident.
The accident took place in the year 2021.

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Mulbagal Govt.
Hospital, R.L.Jalappa Hospital and Victoria Hospital, Bangalore wherein he was treated as an Ismail vs G.S.Narayana on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83602092/
4 inpatient from 27.09.2021 to 14.10.2021, discharged with advice to take follow up treatment.
In this regard, he has produced Ex.P.9 Discharge summary of Victoria Hospital.

Considering that the nature of injuries he has undergone is grievous, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.60,000/
under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.5,00,000/ towards hospitalization,
medical expenses, extra nourishment, conveyance and other miscellaneous expenses etc.,
In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.10 for a sum of Rs.57,999/.
There is no contrary evidence to these bills from the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the said amount under this head.
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner has taken treatment for 18 days at Victoria Hospital which can be made out from Ex.P.8 Discharge summary.

Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and duration of treatment it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least Two months time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.30,000/ under this head.
iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:
On perusal of Ex.P.8/Aadhar Card, the date of birth of the petitioner is 01.01.1975 and the date of accident is 27.09.2021.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is 46 years.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 13.

As such the petitioner is entitled to Rs.11,70,000/
.
(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:
The Petitioner was aged about 46 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained grievous and simple injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 50% functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/ is awarded under this head.
(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospitals, admitted for 18 days as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/
under this head.

(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
Ismail vs G.S.Narayana on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83602092/
5

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the version of the PW.2, the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
In this regard the petitioner or the Pw.2 have not produced any estimation letter.
Therefore, looking to the earlier treatment cost and nature of injuries, evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/ is awarded under this head.

17. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.60,000/
2.

Medical expenses Rs.57,999/
3. Loss of income during laid up Rs.30,000/ period 4. Loss of future income Rs.11,70,000/
5 . Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/ happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/ nourishment charges
7. Future Medical Expenses Rs.20,000/ TOTAL Rs.13,77,999/ If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.13,78,000/ and same is awarded under to the Petitioner.
LIABILITY 18.
The Respondents have not proved their defence as discussed above.
Therefore, the Respondents being the owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.1/insured and has to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner.

The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.30,00,000/
but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.13,78,000/ with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
19. Issue No.3:
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this court proceed to pass the following: ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.13,78,000/ (Rupees Ismail vs G.S.Narayana on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83602092/
6 Thirteen Lakhs Seventy Eight Thousand only) along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The Respondent Nos.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.2/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.

On deposit of compensation and interest, 25% shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner for a period of 3 years in any N/S Bank and the remaining amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of epayment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw decree accordingly.
